response.reading_text: The city of Venice, built on more than 100 small islands in the marshy lagoon of the Adriatic Sea, has a unique history and architecture. Its canals, ornate bridges, and grand piazzas have made it one of the world's most romantic cities. However, this enchanting beauty comes at a price: the city is sinking slowly into the mud due to subsidence caused by the extraction of groundwater over centuries. The authorities are trying to mitigate this problem by pumping out water from beneath the city and injecting cement grout into the soil to stabilize it. Nevertheless, many experts warn that these measures may not be enough to save Venice from further erosion.

questions.question: What is the main reason for Venice's sinking?
options: The city is being flooded by the sea
The extraction of groundwater has caused subsidence
The canals are not deep enough
The buildings are too heavy
questions.answer: The extraction of groundwater has caused subsidence

questions.question: What is being done to stabilize the soil in Venice?
options: Pumping out water from beneath the city and injecting cement grout
Building new bridges to support the city
Draining the canals to reduce water levels
Installing pumps to remove groundwater
questions.answer: Pumping out water from beneath the city and injecting cement grout

questions.question: What is implied about the effectiveness of the measures being taken to save Venice?
options: They are very effective and will completely solve the problem
They may not be enough to save the city from further erosion
They are unnecessary because the city is not sinking
They have already been successful
questions.answer: They may not be enough to save the city from further erosion

questions.question: What does 'subsidence' refer to in this passage?
options: The process of a building sinking into the ground
The extraction of groundwater causing the land to sink
The flooding of the city by the sea
The erosion of the soil due to weathering
questions.answer: The extraction of groundwater causing the land to sink

questions.question: What can be inferred about the author's attitude towards Venice?
options: They think it is a beautiful city and should be preserved
They are concerned about its future due to environmental issues
They believe it is not worth saving because of its problems
They have no opinion on the matter
questions.answer: They are concerned about its future due to environmental issues
